subject: art-design
topicDisplay: Component 2 Investigating The Creative And Cultural Industries
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which formal element is described as a mark made by a moving point, having length and direction?
questions.explain: Line is the path of a moving point and is one of the most basic formal elements.

questions.q: When you give your personal 'interpretation' of an artwork, you are explaining...
options: What you think it means or communicates
questions.explain: Interpretation offers your view of the meaning, message or mood the artwork conveys.

questions.q: What is the secondary colour made by mixing red and yellow?
questions.explain: Red mixed with yellow produces the secondary colour orange.

questions.q: Which textile designer is famous for nature-inspired patterns of the Arts and Crafts movement?
questions.explain: William Morris designed richly patterned, nature-based textiles and wallpapers in the Arts and Crafts style.

questions.q: A 'glaze' on ceramics provides...
options: A glassy, often waterproof and decorative coating
questions.explain: A glaze melts in the kiln to form a glassy surface that seals and decorates the pot.

questions.q: What is casting in sculpture?
options: Pouring liquid material into a mould to set into shape
questions.explain: Casting pours a liquid such as molten metal or plaster into a mould, where it hardens into the form.

questions.q: What is a 'maquette'?
options: A small preliminary model of a sculpture
questions.explain: A maquette is a small-scale model made to plan and test ideas for a larger sculpture.

questions.q: 'Leading' in typography refers to the...
questions.explain: Leading is the vertical spacing between lines of type, affecting readability.

questions.q: 'Surface decoration' in textiles refers to...
options: The way the cloth is woven
The fibre the fabric is made from
Patterns or marks added onto the surface of a fabric
questions.explain: Surface decoration covers techniques such as printing, embroidery or dyeing applied to a fabric's surface.

questions.q: A fast shutter speed is most useful for...
questions.explain: A fast shutter speed freezes rapid action, capturing it as a crisp, sharp image.

questions.q: Which artist created the famous ceiling of the Sistine Chapel during the Renaissance?
questions.explain: Michelangelo painted the Sistine Chapel ceiling, a masterpiece of the Italian Renaissance.

questions.q: Which assessment objective involves responding to the work of other artists?
options: Developing ideas through investigation of sources
questions.explain: Developing ideas requires investigating sources, including the work of relevant artists and cultures.

questions.q: Which is an example of three-dimensional design in everyday life?
options: A product such as a chair
questions.explain: Product design, such as a chair, is a form of three-dimensional design.

questions.q: Impressionism is best known for...
options: Capturing fleeting light and everyday scenes with loose brushwork
questions.explain: Impressionists used loose, visible brushstrokes to capture changing light and ordinary moments.

questions.q: Photographing a subject from directly above is known as a...
questions.explain: A bird's-eye or flat-lay viewpoint looks straight down on the subject from above.

questions.q: Appliqué is a technique that involves...
options: Stitching shaped pieces of fabric onto a larger background cloth
questions.explain: Appliqué sews cut pieces of fabric onto a background to build up an image or pattern.

questions.q: What is 'impasto' in painting?
options: Painting only in black and white
Paint thinned to a watery wash
Thick paint applied so brush or knife marks stand out
questions.explain: Impasto is thickly applied paint that leaves visible, textured marks on the surface.

questions.q: What term describes a range of related colours that sit next to each other on the colour wheel?
questions.explain: Analogous or harmonious colours sit beside each other on the wheel and blend smoothly.

questions.q: What does ISO measure on a camera?
questions.explain: ISO sets the sensor's sensitivity to light; a high ISO brightens images but can add noise.

questions.q: Two-point perspective uses how many vanishing points?
questions.explain: Two-point perspective uses two vanishing points on the horizon, typically for objects seen at a corner.

questions.q: Considering the 'cultural context' of an artwork means thinking about...
options: The time, place and society in which it was made
Just the size of the canvas
questions.explain: Cultural context considers the historical period, place and society that shaped the artwork.

questions.q: 'Saturation' in an image describes...
options: The intensity or purity of the colours
questions.explain: Saturation measures how vivid or intense the colours are; low saturation looks washed out.
